title: Sorting with OrderBy & OrderByDescending
description: Learn to sort collections in ascending and descending order using OrderBy and OrderByDescending.

data.text: Sorting operators arrange the elements of a collection in ascending or descending order. LINQ includes several sorting operators:

rows: Sorts elements in ascending or descending order
Sorts elements in descending order (method syntax only)
Secondary sorting in ascending order (method syntax only)
Secondary sorting in descending order (method syntax only)
Reverses the order of elements (method syntax only)

data.text: `OrderBy` sorts the values of a collection in ascending order by default. Use the `descending` keyword to sort in descending order.

data.title: OrderBy in Query Syntax
data.content: Sorting with OrderBy in query syntax

data.text: The `OrderBy` extension method has two overloads:

data.title: OrderBy Method Signatures
OrderBy in Method Syntax
data.content: Sorting with OrderBy in method syntax

data.text: `OrderByDescending` sorts the collection in descending order. It is **only valid in method syntax** and is not supported in query syntax.

data.title: OrderByDescending
data.code:
var studentsInDescOrder = studentList.OrderByDescending(s => s.StudentName);

// Result: Steve, Ron, Ram, John, Bill

data.text: You can sort on multiple fields separated by commas in query syntax. The collection is first sorted by the first field, and if values are equal, it uses the second field for sorting:

data.title: Multiple Sorting in Query Syntax
Multiple Sorting in Method Syntax
data.text: In method syntax, use `ThenBy` or `ThenByDescending` for secondary sorting after `OrderBy`.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: OrderBy sorts in ascending order by default
Use 'descending' keyword in query syntax for descending order
OrderByDescending is only valid in method syntax
Multiple sorting uses comma-separated fields in query syntax
data.takeaway: Continue to the next lesson to learn about secondary sorting with ThenBy and ThenByDescending.
